analysis:
Reviewed four changed files.

1) LaunchAgent.swift (head lines 288-300): three env keys are added to the launchd passthrough allowlist: GlobalKVCacheBudget.idleCacheSweepEnvironmentKey, EngineV2Factory.segmentRetentionEnvironmentKey and EngineV2Factory.segmentHostZerosEnvironmentKey. Only allowlisted, non-empty values reach the plist. The keys are fixed constants and cannot be injected by a remote party; this is a local operator knob. The passthrough is operator rollback plumbing, not a new privilege. Retained host-zeroed paged KV segments (SEGMENT_RETENTION and SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS) relate to T-028 (residual KV data) and T-041, but the changed file only carries the opt-out; the retention and zeroing implementation is outside the supplied evidence. Next pass should confirm that retention defaults and host zeroing preserve the T-028 posture, and that retained segments are not reusable across cache scopes or salts.

2) StartupPreloader.swift: adds an optional reclaimBeforeSkip hook, called once when free memory is below the requirement, and then re-samples the requirement and free memory. The 'no eviction' design is preserved by the code path (lines 153-159). The hook is an injected closure, and its production wiring (ProviderLoop+StartupPreload) is not supplied. Remaining question: confirm the production reclaim only flushes free KV segments and the MLX buffer cache and does not evict loaded models. This is an availability and memory-admission concern (T-029/T-010 class), not a confidentiality one. The guard still fails closed to skip, so there is no security regression.

3) EngineV2TestStubs.swift: test-only change adding an onShutdown parameter.

4) KVPoolIdleSweepTests.swift: new test file (only the patch excerpt was visible and there is no head text), so its content is partially unexamined. It covers sweep window policy and appears to be tests only.

No changes touch the coordinator websocket, attestation, keys or SSD cache crypto. No concrete regression identified.
